    },

      "severity": "medium",
      "title": "Memory profile contradicts eager allocation",
      "body": "The docstring claims a peak below 4 MB for 10 million records because only one batch is retained. The implementation materializes the entire iterable and every batch simultaneously.       "file": "docs/audits/fixtures/metrics-uploader/uploader.py",
      "line_start": 3,

      "confidence": 1,
      "recommendation": "Replace the claim with a reproducible measurement and document linear memory usage. If bounded memory is intended, yield batches incrementally and measure a consumer that releases each batch."
    }

  "next_steps": [
    "Fix batching and quota arithmetic, correct the memory documentation, and rerun tests with the failing boundary cases."
  ]

result.summary: Do not ship: batches exceed the API cap, quota validation accepts exactly 10% reserve, and the documented memory profile is false. All five existing tests pass despite these defects.

findings.title: Batch size exceeds the API's 256-record limit
findings.body: BATCH_SIZE is 265. make_batches(range(1000)) produces lengths [265, 265, 265, 205], making three batches unacceptable to the API. Existing tests check batch count and total records but never enforce the API cap.
findings.recommendation: Set the size to 256. Test inputs around 256 and assert every batch contains at most 256 records while preserving the complete input sequence.

findings.title: Floating-point rounding admits a forbidden quota split
findings.body: check_quota_split([0.3, 0.3, 0.3]) returns 0.10000000000000009 instead of raising, although the intended shares allocate 90% and leave exactly 10%. Reproduced on Python 3.9 and 3.14. The corresponding test explicitly requires this incorrect acceptance. The guard also accepts NaN because its comparison is false.
findings.recommendation: Define quota precision using decimal arithmetic or integer units, reject non-finite inputs, and enforce the strict boundary. Replace the three-equal-shares acceptance test with rejection and cover reserves below, exactly at, and above 10%.

findings.title: Memory profile contradicts eager allocation
findings.body: The docstring claims a peak below 4 MB for 10 million records because only one batch is retained. The implementation materializes the entire iterable and every batch simultaneously. A tracemalloc probe with 10 million repeated None values peaked at 162,424,448 bytes, even without allocating individual record objects. Consumers relying on the documented bound could exhaust memory.
findings.recommendation: Replace the claim with a reproducible measurement and document linear memory usage. If bounded memory is intended, yield batches incrementally and measure a consumer that releases each batch.

next_steps: Fix batching and quota arithmetic, correct the memory documentation, and rerun tests with the failing boundary cases.
